transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-12-07
Start: 15:00 UTC / 10:00 ET
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SRE); Alex (Rivermark CTO), Priya (Infra), Jordan (ML), Tina (PM)

Summary:
Quick sync of POC weekly check-in focused on latency tuning. Reviewed TTFT (time to first token) numbers, streaming vs chunked responses, sequence length distribution, and kernel choice impacts. Agreed to run kernel matrix and share raw traces. Next sync scheduled.

Topics:
- TTFT regressions after switching to streaming pipeline
- Preferential kernel choices for 8k seq vs 1k seq workloads
- Batching, prefix/KV cache benefits, and quantization tradeoffs
- Security/production traces sharing (S3 upload, redacted)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we got 40 minutes so we will focus on latency numbers first, then actions. alex, anything new on your side?
[00:10] Alex: yeah thanks samir, priya and i did another run overnight, we saw TTFT jump from ~85ms to 170ms for streaming requests when we pushed a config change, not sure if it's client side or the runtime, there was also more variability at p95
[00:25] Priya: yeah it looked like the first chunk is delayed, maybe the request isn't flagged for streaming quickly enough, we send a 512 token prompt then stream response, so first token matters a lot for UX
[00:38] Lina: okay that matches something we saw - when streaming negotiation or handshake hits a slow path we fall back to non-streamed generation for the first token then resume, that can double TTFT; i'll check the handshake logs, sometimes the router does an extra model compatibility probe
[00:55] Jordan: curious - are you seeing this on both hosted and dedicated? our tests are on the dedicated pool you provided.
[01:05] Samir: good call - this POC is dedicated, right? alex: yes dedicated-internal. so kernels and batch packing matter, less noisy than hosted but still tunable
[01:18] Marcus: quick note: we pushed a kernel patch last week that changed the scheduling window, might affect packing behavior at small sequence lengths, low-level scheduling can shift TTFT vs throughput tradeoff
[01:32] Alex: right, and our sequences vary - ~60% are short (<=128 tokens), 30% mid (128-1024), 10% long (up to 4096). so any optimization for 8k sequences isn't worth it if it regresses short seq latency
[01:50] Lina: perfect, that's the distribution we asked for, we'll prioritize short-seq fast-paths - that often means smaller batch sizes and kernel choices optimized for low-latency single-query execution, like fused attention kernels vs generic matmul kernels
[02:05] Priya: can you explain kernel choices a bit more? we've seen references to triton kernels, cuBLAS and also some Redwood in-house kernels in previous docs
[02:15] Lina: yeah short version: cuBLAS/MatMul works well for throughput, Triton/fused kernels and attention-specific kernels (we sometimes call them "fused-attn") can reduce per-token latency for short sequences because they avoid extra memory copies and have better scheduling for the KV cache; but they are sensitive to sequence length and batch size
[02:40] Alex: are there regression risks with fused kernels, like correctness or higher memory?
[02:45] Lina: small risk on very long sequences and some edge-case ops, but we run model validation; memory can be higher but for short seq it's fine; we can toggle kernel at runtime per-request or route by policy
[03:00] Jordan: we also noticed p50 is okay but p95 spikes when there are concurrent large eval jobs overnight, could be contention on the node's memory bandwidth
[03:15] Marcus: yep contention - two levers: isolate heavy batches to separate queues or enforce rate limits on background jobs; autoscaler can also pin capacity for reserved slots
[03:28] Samir: back to TTFT - we recorded traces, lina, did you look at the handshake and router traces?
[03:34] Lina: i pulled the initial traces, there's a ~60ms delay in the router before streaming chunks start, which is the extra compatibility check i mentioned; i'll correlate with Marcus's kernel schedule changes
[03:45] Alex: is that something we can disable? we are comfortable with model variant mapping, we don't need extra probes in the middle of a request
[03:52] Lina: yes we can skip the probe for pinned models or when the route has a canary flag off - we'll propose a safe toggle
[04:02] Priya: that would help. Also, on our side we could reduce initial client buffer from 512 to 256 tokens to make the first chunk smaller - any downside?
[04:11] Lina: smaller initial chunk lowers TTFT because first chunk transmits faster, but you increase total number of chunks; for UX first token matters more, so usually good tradeoff
[04:24] Alex: we tried smaller chunk and saw ~20% TTFT improvement but throughput dropped a bit, acceptable for chat.
[04:35] Samir: good. let's talk about quantization - any wins there for latency?
[04:40] Lina: quantization often lowers memory and can speedup via better cache behavior, but on some hardware quantization can add dequant/requant overhead for small sequences; recommendation: run bench with and without quant, we do automated quant profiles per model
[04:55] Jordan: we did an int8 profile and saw mixed results, sometimes slower at <=128 tokens, faster at long sequences - seems consistent with what you're saying
[05:08] Marcus: also check KV cache warmup - if the cache miss rate is high, first tokens will be slower; prefix caching helps a lot for repeated prompts, we can enable prefix/KV caching per-route
[05:20] Priya: can you explain prefix/KV cache a bit? we saw a 30% p95 win on a demo last month but don't know how it applies to our varying prompts
[05:30] Lina: prefix caching stores the tokenized prefix and KV pairs so repeated prompts don't recompute prefix attention; for many assistants with shared context it helps, for highly dynamic prompts it's less effective; we'll simulate with your trace sample set
[05:45] Alex: what's the easiest quick wins we can implement before the next sync?
[05:50] Samir: shortlist: 1) disable router probe for pinned model, 2) smaller initial streaming chunk on client, 3) enable prefix caching for top 20% repeated templates, 4) run kernel matrix to choose fused vs matmul kernel for short seqs
[06:05] Jordan: sounds good - for 1) we need an RFC from redwood describing any safety implications
[06:13] Samir: we'll prepare a short note, lina will author.
[06:17] Lina: noted, i'll include rollback steps and metrics to watch (TTFT p50/p95, chunk latency, cpu/gpu util).
[06:25] Priya: regarding traces - we will redacted user data, upload to the shared S3, can you provide the exact path and retention policy?
[06:33] Marcus: yes we'll create a temporary bucket path with limited retention and tight IAM, samir will share link; we only need 48 hours of samples to reproduce patterns
[06:42] Alex: FYI we also have an internal compliance review - SOC2 questions popped up about audit logs for model access. will that affect anything with dedicated?
[06:52] Samir: dedicated supports audit logs and KMS - we'll include our security pack and SOC2 artifact, but if you need on-prem private control plane that is a different product discussion
[07:05] Tina: timeline question - what's realistic to see measurable p95 improvements?
[07:10] Lina: low-hanging config changes and routing toggles - you could see improvements within 48-72 hours after we push toggles and you run the test harness; kernel-level changes and deeper tuning might take 1-2 weeks for validation
[07:22] Alex: ok target - get quick wins done by next sync, kernel matrix results within two weeks
[07:29] Samir: agreed. Lina, Marcus, any additional measurement you want from rivermark?
[07:36] Marcus: please include high-fidelity traces with headers including request size, prompt token count, client chunk size, model variant, and whether streaming flag was present; that helps us correlate
[07:48] Priya: we can add those, will anonymize PII fields.
[07:53] Jordan: one more question - do you have a recommended autoscaler tune for low-latency workloads? we saw autoscaler sometimes batch more aggressively to save cost which hurts TTFT
[08:03] Lina: yes, for low-latency we use aggressive min replicas and tighter batch timeouts; basically favor p95 SLO over cost savings, we can propose a profile for your traffic mix
[08:16] Alex: please include cost estimate for switching to low-latency profile vs current config
[08:21] Samir: will include in the spreadsheet.
[08:25] Tina: great. let's recap next steps and owners.
[08:28] Samir: recap: samir share runbook + pricing spreadsheet; lina run kernel matrix and router-probe toggle plan; marcus enable p95 tracing and create S3 path; alex to upload traces and verify; schedule next sync 2028-12-14 14:00 ET. is that captured?
[08:42] Alex: yes captured. thanks everyone.
[08:45] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and tickets.

End of transcript.
